LoloBuy customized product guide: confirm before paying

A custom order turns your instructions into the product specification. Before payment, make every variable clear enough for the seller, shopping agent and warehouse to understand without guessing.

Editorial note: This independent guide is based on LoloBuy’s public customized-product, purchasing, order-modification, confirmation, inspection and return materials, checked on 20 October 2026. Seller capabilities, prices, production steps and return decisions can change. Confirm every material term on the live order rather than treating this page as a promise.

Can LoloBuy buy a customized product?

LoloBuy’s current help material says its shopping agent can purchase customized products. It directs buyers to put special requirements in “leave a message to seller.” The same page says LoloBuy may contact the buyer to confirm the customized content. When pictures are necessary, the official instruction is to send the images and requirements to customer service and include the item code.

That answers whether a customized order can enter the workflow, but not whether any seller can produce any design. A seller may limit dimensions, colours, fonts, materials, production methods or image formats. Stock, price and domestic delivery shown for a standard option may not apply to a personalized version. The useful buyer question is therefore not simply “Is customization supported?” It is “Can this exact specification be confirmed before the agent commits my payment?”

A good LoloBuy custom order creates one version of the truth. The seller listing, your written remarks, any artwork file and the agent’s confirmation should describe the same output. If they conflict, pause and ask which record controls the purchase.

Separate the base product from the custom work

Start by identifying the ordinary product before describing the change. Save the direct seller link, listing title, seller name, selected base colour, size, model, material and quantity. Then place customization in a separate block. This prevents a long design note from hiding a wrong underlying option.

For example, “black canvas tote, large size, one unit” identifies the base item. “Print the supplied white logo, centred on front, maximum width 18 cm” describes the requested work. If the seller offers several printing methods, record the named method instead of writing only “high quality.” If the listing does not state the method, ask; do not infer embroidery, screen printing, engraving or heat transfer from a promotional photograph.

Use the seller’s original option wording alongside an English explanation. Machine translation can collapse meaningful differences between “one side,” “two sides,” “text only,” “image plus text,” “sample” and “final product.” Retaining the original label gives the purchasing agent an exact option to match.

Write a specification that can be checked

A practical specification covers only facts that affect the result:

Content: the exact spelling, capitalization, punctuation, date or number to reproduce.
Placement: front, back, left, right, centre or another seller-supported location.
Size: dimensions and units, with a tolerance only if the seller agrees to one.
Appearance: seller colour name or code, font name, finish and orientation where offered.
Base option: item colour, size, model and material selected from the listing.
Quantity: number of finished seller units, not the number of design elements.
File reference: filename and version date for every image or artwork supplied.
Stop condition: what requires your approval instead of an automatic substitute.

Copy text directly from a prepared note. Names, dates and numbers are easy to mistype in a checkout field. Check confusing characters such as O and 0, I and l, hyphens, accents and non-Latin scripts. If line breaks matter, show them explicitly. “Line 1: NORTH / Line 2: 2026” is harder to misread than a sentence describing the layout.

Use one measurement system consistently. If the listing is in centimetres, avoid mixing inches into the same instruction unless you provide a verified conversion. For fitted items, distinguish body measurements, finished-product measurements and the seller’s standard size. The size and variant checklist can help separate these fields.

Control images and artwork versions

The official customized-product page provides a route for sending pictures and says to identify the relevant item code. Treat that code as the link between the file and the order. A generic message such as “use the logo I sent” is unsafe when you have several orders, colours or file versions.

Name each file clearly, such as “tote-logo-front-v3.png.” In the order remark, repeat the filename, intended side, orientation and approximate printed size. If colour accuracy matters, give the seller-supported colour reference and accept that screen previews alone cannot prove the physical result. Do not send two alternative files unless the note clearly says which one is approved.

Check whether the seller requires a particular format, resolution, background treatment or outline conversion. LoloBuy’s public page confirms that pictures can accompany requirements; it does not publish universal artwork specifications. Those production details must come from the seller. Never assume that a low-resolution preview will be redrawn, that a transparent background will remain transparent or that the seller will correct your spelling.

Ask for confirmation before purchase

Turn uncertainty into short questions with decision consequences. Ask whether the chosen price includes the custom work, whether setup or domestic shipping changes the total, whether the seller can reproduce the requested language, and whether a proof is available before production. Ask what happens if the selected base option is unavailable.

A useful stop instruction is: “Do not substitute the base colour, alter the artwork or accept a higher total without my confirmation.” This does not force a seller to hold stock or create a proof. It tells the agent when not to guess.

LoloBuy explains that an order can show “Pending for Confirmation” when product information needs verification. If that happens, read the order-page instruction and answer the exact issue. Keep your reply consistent with the saved specification. A new file, changed spelling or different size is a revision, not a clarification, and may require the agent to ask the seller again.

Know when changes become difficult

LoloBuy’s modification guidance distinguishes orders by seller dispatch. Before dispatch, the agent can try to negotiate a modification. After dispatch, LoloBuy says modification generally cannot be negotiated at that stage; a buyer who insists on a different option may need to wait for warehouse arrival, request a return and place another order, with related domestic return costs.

For a customized item, production may begin before the parcel is physically dispatched. The public help pages do not promise a universal edit window for personalized work. The sensible approach is to treat the confirmed specification as final once purchasing begins. If you notice an error, contact the order agent immediately, but do not assume the seller can stop or remake the item.

Likewise, do not build the purchase around an assumed right to return. LoloBuy’s public return materials state that seller agreement, product condition, timing, packaging and fees can affect a request. They do not create a special guaranteed return right for customized goods. Check the live seller listing and obtain a clear answer before payment if return eligibility would determine whether you buy.

Understand what warehouse QC can prove

Warehouse photographs can be useful, but they are not a production test. LoloBuy’s published inspection scope covers visible information such as style, quantity, colour, size and model. It excludes authenticity, functionality, professional product quality and internal details of many sealed products.

Translate your specification into observable checks: the printed name is visible, the base colour appears to match, one logo is on the requested side, and the stated model or size tag is present. For small text, precise dimensions, engraving depth, colour matching or fine alignment, ask whether the seller or LoloBuy currently offers a suitable close-up or measurement service before relying on it.

A photograph can show that text exists; it may not prove exact colour, durability, adhesion, fabric feel or performance. Electronics, digital products and accessories are specifically outside the published professional inspection scope. Do not ask a warehouse photo to certify properties it cannot observe.

Pre-payment checklist

Listing: The direct link opens and the chosen base option is still available.
Specification: Text, placement, dimensions, colour, method and quantity are explicit.
Artwork: One approved file is named, oriented and tied to the item code.
Price: The total and Chinese domestic delivery reflect the customized version, not only the base item.
Proof: Any seller proof or approval step is documented, without assuming one exists.
Substitution: The agent knows which changes require your approval.
Returns: You have checked current seller terms instead of assuming a customized item can be returned.
QC: Requested warehouse checks are visible and within the published inspection scope.

A concise custom-order note

Base product: black canvas tote, large, quantity 1
Seller option: original option label plus English meaning
Customization: print approved white artwork on front centre, maximum width 18 cm
Artwork: tote-logo-front-v3.png, item code included in customer-service message
Exact text: none beyond the supplied artwork
Confirm before buying: final price includes one-side printing; seller accepts PNG file
Do not substitute: no different colour, size, artwork or print method without approval
Warehouse check: front artwork visible, base colour and size label match order

Conclusion: make customization unambiguous

A reliable LoloBuy customized product order is a controlled specification, not a loose collection of messages. Identify the base product, preserve the seller’s option, write measurable requirements, connect the correct artwork to the item code, define stop conditions and answer confirmation requests consistently.

Customization always leaves some facts outside ordinary warehouse inspection. If the seller cannot confirm a decision-critical detail before payment, a clearer listing or standard product may be the better choice. To research products before preparing the specification, open FindSpreadsheet →
